result.rationale: The schema (`guests: z.array(z.string().email())`) has no uniqueness/length refinement, and the handler's `uniqueGuests` filter only removes emails matching existing attendees or the blacklist — it does not dedupe within the input array. So a single request with duplicate emails passes validation and `createMany` inserts duplicate attendee rows. Only the client-side dialog enforces uniqueness, which the server trusts. This is verifiable in the diff and is a real correctness defect.

record.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.schema.ts:5 — No schema test for an empty guests array, duplicates, or a max length, and the server doesn't dedupe the input array, so duplicate attendees can be created.

adjudication.rationale: The server-side ZAddGuestsInputSchema only validates that `guests` is an array of emails (no uniqueness/min/max). In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `uniqueGuests` filters out existing attendees and blacklisted emails but does NOT dedupe duplicates within the incoming `guests` array. That means an input like `["a@b.com","a@b.com"]` (not already an attendee) will produce two entries in `guestsFullDetails` and `createMany` will attempt to create duplicate attendee rows. The UI adds a uniqueness refine, but it can be bypassed by calling the TRPC endpoint directly.
